records.scope_text:
范围片段1: The relationship between packet arrival time and data redundancy is complex, as increasing data redundancy can both improve and worsen packet arrival times. On the one hand, adding redundancy to a transmission can increase the amount of data that needs to be transmitted, which can increase the overall time it takes for packets to arrive. This is because each packet must carry additional information that must be transmitted and received. On the other hand, data redundancy can also improve packet arrival times by helping to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the data being transmitted. By including error-correcting codes and other forms of redundancy, data can be checked and cor- rected for errors before it is transmitted, reducing the need for retransmissions and improving overall network efﬁ- ciency. In general, the relationship between packet arrival time and data redundancy will depend on a variety of factors, including the speciﬁc application, the network environment, and the amount of redundancy being used. By carefully balancing the need for data redundancy with the need for efﬁcient and timely packet transmission, net- work engineers can optimize network performance and ensure reliable data transmission [ 30]

By isolating this fault, engineers can work to repair or replace the affected components and restore the system to its proper functioning. In this way, jitter and fault isolation are closely related. Jitter can be both a symptom of a fault and a tool for identifying the source of the fault. By monitoring and analyzing jitter, engineers can improve the reliability and performance of electronic systems, and ensure that faults are quickly and accurately isolated and addressed [ 27]
